description: Follow-up to defk-4b2 (which bounds owned bytes per call with max_owned but does not free early). The ticket's case v = copy(v) never frees: the old buffer is either still seen by another binding or not owned. The buffers that die are earlier per-iteration copies (b = a; a[i] = x; ... b[0]: the previous iteration's copy dies when b is rebound). Needs: (1) a must-not-alias/ownership analysis proving a buffer has no live binding, is not an accumulator's or returned value and is not held across a branch join, across iterations (the compiler today tracks only may-share via carried/2 and shared?); (2) a runtime defk_disown(ctx, slot) releasing the binary, NULLing the slot and subtracting owned_bytes, with array values carrying their slot index (defk_make_arr scans linearly today); (3) resume safety for spilled locals; (4) forced-yield and property tests on the freed paths.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Triage (2026-10-11): ready-for-human. Low priority: the max_owned budget (defk-4b2) already keeps a per-iteration copy or alloc from taking the node down. Early freeing needs a new must-not-alias analysis; a design call for the maintainer before any agent work.

Design proposal (2026-10-22, for the owner's call; nothing implemented).

**Demand.** No example and no docs/performance.md entry shows the "each iteration keeps a buffer" report note today. The one real case (defk-33b) was a bug whose copy was removed, and max_owned (defk-4b2) bounds the class. Deferring until a catalog workload hits the budget is a legitimate answer.

**What the trace found (lib/defk/copies.ex, compiler.ex array values / reduce accumulators / calls).**
1. The alias classes are may-share and already cover branch joins (branch_val merges the arms' bufs into one class, flow-insensitively). An inlined callee's array parameter keeps the caller's buf ref (array_binding keeps v[:buf]). Pointer moves (b = a, swaps, call results) keep the buf. So "no binding whose class is the dying buffer's is live after the block" is a sound must-not-alias test at a block exit, with ONE gap:
2. acc_env gives an array accumulator a FRESH buf (carried(make_ref(), a[:buf])) whether or not loop_owned copied the initial value. When it did not copy, one physical buffer has two refs (the dead outer binding's and the accumulator's); `carried` records provenance for unreturned_writes!, not aliasing. Today harmless (the outer binding is dead, else loop_owned copied). For freeing it must become one ref: reuse a.buf when no copy was made, or merge the two into one class. That is the whole "new analysis": one fact at one site, not a second tracker.
3. The ticket's own case, two iterations of `{a, n} = for ..., reduce: {a, 0} do b = a; a[i] = x; ...b[0]...; {a, n+1} end`: iteration k: b = a (buf X, pointer move); a[i] = x copies (b live) -> a = Z carried from X; body value = {Z, _}. At body exit b (X) is bound in the body (depth = body depth), owned, and X is in no class of the escape set (acc new value Z, scope.out) -> X is dead -> free. Next iteration repeats with Z in b's place. With a write in a branch, the arm's copy and the old buf are one merged class -> the escape set holds it -> not freed (conservative, correct). `v = copy(v)` at a write never frees: the old buf is by construction still seen by a live binding.
4. Free point: a nested block whose env is discarded at its end. Arms do not go through leave/2 (only a plain __block__ does, compiler.ex lower_expr_env), so the uniform rule is: at the end of an arm, a loop body (for, reduce, reduce_while/all?/any? fn) and an inlined callee's body, release every binding bound at that block's depth that is owned and whose class is not in {scope.out classes} ∪ {the block's value classes (tuple elements too)}. The kernel's own body needs nothing (defk_finish). A plain nested block binds into the outer, so no free there.

**Runtime shape.** `defk_disown(ctx, data)`: backward scan of ctx->owned for data (recent buffers die first), enif_release_binary, owned_bytes -= size, data = NULL, and a free list threaded through the NULL slots (next index in `size`, head in ctx) that defk_own_raw pops first. Without reuse nowned grows ~24 B per iteration for ever. defk_release_owned already skips NULL; defk_make_arr never matches NULL; the bits accumulator's slot1 and defk_bind's copy_slot index slots that are never freed, so reuse cannot invalidate them. Reject a slot index inside defk_arr_T (three words, every array op signature).

**Resume.** A freed binding's C local is stale at the next spill, but a spill is a store, never a dereference, and the binding is rebound before any read. To confirm under DEFK_SANITIZE=address with __defk_force_yields__.

**The discriminating question: the budget agreement.** docs/language.md promises native owned bytes >= Elixir mode's alloc sum ("never the reverse"), and defk-4b2 decided an alloc in a loop raises at the same iteration in both modes. Freeing dead allocs natively inverts both. Freeing dead copies never does (Elixir mode does not count copies).
  (A) Free dead copies only, natively. Zero agreement risk, no Elixir mode change. Needs an origin tag on the buf (copy vs alloc; a merged class is never freed anyway). Covers the ticket's case. Dead allocs in a loop stay as today: the report already says to hoist the alloc, which the user can do; a per-iteration copy the user cannot code around.
  (B) Also free dead allocs, mirrored in Elixir mode: the decision is static (binding, block exit), so Elixir mode subtracts byte_size(binding) from owned_call's {used, max} at the same point for alloc-origin bindings. Keeps "same iteration" agreement, more surface (ElixirMode translation, Ops), and a merged class with an alloc member still cannot be freed.
  Recommendation: (A) first if the ticket is taken at all; (B) as a follow-up only when a workload shows a per-iteration alloc that cannot be hoisted.

**Tests.** test/owned_budget_test.exs (8 KiB budget): a dead per-iteration copy no longer raises; the live-copy loop raises at the same iteration as today; agreement under forced yields; one StreamData property over loop lengths and branch shapes; one ASan run. Report note text changes ("freed at the end of each iteration" beside the existing note): mix defk.docs. Surfaces: docs/language.md Copies and budget sections, CHANGELOG (promised surface: the budget text), an ADR for the free rule and the one-ref invariant.

**Owner's call.** (1) defer, or take it; (2) if taken: A or B; (3) free point: all three nested-block exits (recommended, one helper) or loop bodies only.

Decision (2026-10-22, owner): copies only. Free dead copy-origin buffers natively at the three nested-block exits (arm, loop body, inlined callee body); allocs stay until return (Elixir mode's budget agreement unchanged). Accumulators without a copy keep the source's buf ref (the one-ref invariant).

title: Free dead owned buffers early, so a per-iteration copy or alloc no longer accumulates until return
